v1_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled since August 2026 (610→1260/month, E-04). A confirmed contributing mechanism is that manual meter-reading route completion fell below target (0.88 vs 0.95 target, 9200 accounts, E-06) during Aug-Sep, causing estimate-substituted bills for those accounts, which drives the ESTIMATED-read share of disputes (1240 bills, E-01). However the majority of disputed bills (1785/3025, 59%) carry an ACTUAL read type (E-01), so this mechanism explains only part of the surge; the cause of disputes on actual-read bills is not yet established by current evidence.
v2_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled since August 2026 (610→1260/month, E-04). The best-supported mechanism is a billing-import validation rule change: rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 coincident with the surge onset (E-12), compares raw register values directly against 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling and rejects accepted AMI reads as high-consumption; this rejection-and-estimate-substitution accounts for 1184 of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (95%, E-11). This mechanism explains the ESTIMATED-read share of disputes (41%) but not the majority of disputed bills (1785/3025, 59%) that carry an ACTUAL read type (E-01); the cause of disputes on actual-read bills remains unestablished by current evidence.
